{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01X8BcgNvpm3s4qU54dax1wU","type":"tool_result","content":"740\t  (tenant-provisioning-command.service.ts:389-400). After a SUPER_ADMIN removes a module from a\n741\t  tenant, that tenant's MODULE_USERs/MODULE_MANAGERs keep the module in their login modules list and\n742\t  pass the shell's hasModuleAccess gate; their existing role permissions also persist (entitlement\n743\t  is checked only at grant time, capability-authority.ts:164-201), so backend requests keep\n744\t  succeeding on unchanged JWT permission claims. The disable toggle the admin panel exposes is\n745\t  therefore only partially enforced.\n746\t- **Evidence:**\n747\t  - `apps/auth-service/src/modules/authentication/services/token.service.ts:436-448`\n748\t  - `apps/auth-service/src/modules/tenant/services/tenant-provisioning-command.service.ts:389-400`\n749\t  - `apps/auth-service/src/modules/tenant/services/capability-authority.ts:145-201`\n750\t  - `web/shell/src/App.tsx:116-119`\n751\t  - `web/shared-ui/src/contexts/AuthContext.tsx:658-663`\n752\t- **Verification:** Confirmed by direct read. (1) token.service.ts getUserModules: the TENANT_ADMIN\n753\t  branch (421-435) joins tenant_modules WHERE isEnabled=true, but the non-admin else-branch\n754\t  (436-448) reads only userModuleAssignmentRepository (isActive + expiry) with relations ['module']\n755\t  — no tenant_modules join. (2) removeTenantModule (tenant-provisioning-command.service.ts:381-406)\n756\t  flips only tenant_modules.isEnabled=false; the full admin-panel chain (admin-api\n757\t  modules.controller.ts:207 → modules.service.ts:698 → NATS client → auth-service) confirms this is\n758\t  the disable path. (3) FE: roleHasModuleAccess (AuthContext.tsx:175-181) gates non-admins on the\n759\t  modules claim, so they keep menu+route access FOREVER, including fresh logins. One sub-claim\n760\t  REFUTED: resourcePermissions IS intersected with resolveEntitledCapabilities at every mint\n761\t  (token.service.ts:621-635, RBAC-HIGH-010), so capability-gated endpoints revoke within ≤15m token\n762\t  TTL + 60s cache — the auditor's 'entitlement checked only at grant time' is wrong. However the\n763\t  backend hole survives via a broader mechanism the auditor missed: @RequireTenantPermission appears\n764\t  in only 5 services and farm-service has ZERO occurrences — its resolvers use only\n765\t  GqlAuthGuard/JwtAuthGuard/TenantGuard/MobileFeatureGuard (role+tenant, unchanged by disable), and\n766\t  no server-side guard consumes the modules JWT claim (tenant-isolation.guard.ts:233 merely copies\n767\t  it into context). So a MODULE_USER retains indefinite working FE+BE access to a disabled module's\n768\t  role-gated surface (nearly all of farm-service). HIGH is correct: a SUPER_ADMIN admin-panel\n769\t  control is silently ineffective for the majority of tenant users, and the codebase itself declares\n770\t  module entitlement a revenue-integrity invariant (capability-authority.ts:52-56).\n771\t- **Root cause:** The entitlement invariant (tenant_modules.isEnabled gates everything for the\n772\t  tenant) was retrofitted point-by-point — TENANT_ADMIN menu branch, grant-time\n773\t  CapabilityAuthorityService, mint-time resourcePermissions intersection (RBAC-HIGH-010) — but there\n774\t  is no single SSoT resolver for 'effective module access', so two paths never received the check:\n775\t  (a) the non-admin modules claim reads user_module_assignments alone (token.service.ts:436-448 — it\n776\t  treats the assignment table as the whole truth when the contract is tenant-licensed AND\n777\t  user-assigned), and (b) nothing enforces module entitlement at request time on role-gated-only\n778\t  surfaces — the modules JWT claim is consumed by zero backend guards and farm-service (plus most\n779\t  module services) has no @RequireTenantPermission usage, so RolesGuard/TenantGuard pass on claims a\n780\t  module disable never changes. removeTenantModule not touching user_module_assignments is NOT\n781\t  itself the bug — assignments should survive a disable so re-enable restores them; the bug is that\n782\t  read/enforce paths derive access from the assignment table without intersecting the tenant\n783\t  entitlement SSoT.\n784\t- **Fix design:** Systemic class: 'entitlement enforced at grant/mint time but not on every\n785\t  read/request path' — fix at the pattern level with one SSoT + one declarative guard, NOT by\n786\t  syncing/deleting assignment rows (state duplication would break re-enable and re-introduce drift).\n787\t  Leg 1 — make the modules claim automatically entitlement-correct (Tier 2): add a\n788\t  USER_EFFECTIVE_MODULES_SQL next to ENABLED_MODULE_CODES_SQL in permission-catalogue.ts (SSoT:\n789\t  user_module_assignments ura JOIN tenant_modules tm ON tm.\"moduleId\"=ura.\"moduleId\" AND\n790\t  tm.\"tenantId\"=$2 AND tm.\"isEnabled\"=true JOIN modules m ON m.id=ura.\"moduleId\" AND\n791\t  m.\"isActive\"=true WHERE ura.\"userId\"=$1 AND ura.\"isActive\"=true AND (ura.\"expiresAt\" IS NULL OR\n792\t  ura.\"expiresAt\">NOW()), selecting code/name/defaultRoute). Replace the token.service.ts\n793\t  else-branch repository read (436-448) with this query, and replace the identical unfiltered read\n794\t  in tenant-admin.service.ts:166 with the same SSoT so the tenant-admin UI and the JWT claim cannot\n795\t  disagree. This fixes menus, shell hasModuleAccess gating, and login redirect for non-admins within\n796\t  the existing 60s module-cache TTL, and re-enable restores access with no re-assignment. Leg 2 —\n797\t  make request-time enforcement automatic for whole module services (Tier 2, closes the farm-service\n798\t  hole): new ModuleEntitlementGuard in libs/backend-common (guards/module-entitlement.guard.ts)\n799\t  registered as APP_GUARD via a static forRoot({ moduleCode }) in each tenant-scoped module"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"9be46226-3b69-499a-bac9-9a3f4e17b5c0","uuid":"8837c690-7e7d-4f0a-8974-5250865c6102","timestamp":"2026-09-21T03:27:19.231Z","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/home/gharunner/actions-runner/_work/aquaculture_platform/aquaculture_platform/aria-worktrees/req-AIR-aria-evidence-judge-a2a774f21b9d/docs/reviews/claude/2026-07-20-admin-panel-e2e-audit/findings/modules.md","content":"  (tenant-provisioning-command.service.ts:389-400). (2) removeTenantModule (tenant-provisioning-command.service.ts:381-406)\n  flips only tenant_modules.isEnabled=false; the full admin-panel chain (admin-api\n  modules.controller.ts:207 → modules.service.ts:698 → NATS client → auth-service) confirms this is\n  the disable path. However the\n  backend hole survives via a broader mechanism the auditor missed: @RequireTenantPermission appears\n  in only 5 services and farm-service has ZERO occurrences — its resolvers use only\n  GqlAuthGuard/JwtAuthGuard/TenantGuard/MobileFeatureGuard (role+tenant, unchanged by disable), and\n  no server-side guard consumes the modules JWT claim (tenant-isolation.guard.ts:233 merely copies\n  it into context). So a MODULE_USER retains indefinite working FE+BE access to a disabled module's\n  role-gated surface (nearly all of farm-service). HIGH is correct: a SUPER_ADMIN admin-panel\n  control is silently ineffective for the majority of tenant users, and the codebase itself declares\n  module entitlement a revenue-integrity invariant (capability-authority.ts:52-56).\n- **Root cause:** The entitlement invariant (tenant_modules.isEnabled gates everything for the\n  tenant) was retrofitted point-by-point — TENANT_ADMIN menu branch, grant-time\n  CapabilityAuthorityService, mint-time resourcePermissions intersection (RBAC-HIGH-010) — but there\n  is no single SSoT resolver for 'effective module access', so two paths never received the check:\n  (a) the non-admin modules claim reads user_module_assignments alone (token.service.ts:436-448 — it\n  treats the assignment table as the whole truth when the contract is tenant-licensed AND\n  user-assigned), and (b) nothing enforces module entitlement at request time on role-gated-only\n  surfaces — the modules JWT claim is consumed by zero backend guards and farm-service (plus most\n  module services) has no @RequireTenantPermission usage, so RolesGuard/TenantGuard pass on claims a\n  module disable never changes. removeTenantModule not touching user_module_assignments is NOT\n  itself the bug — assignments should survive a disable so re-enable restores them; the bug is that\n  read/enforce paths derive access from the assignment table without intersecting the tenant\n  entitlement SSoT.\n- **Fix design:** Systemic class: 'entitlement enforced at grant/mint time but not on every\n  read/request path' — fix at the pattern level with one SSoT + one declarative guard, NOT by\n  syncing/deleting assignment rows (state duplication would break re-enable and re-introduce drift).\n  Leg 1 — make the modules claim automatically entitlement-correct (Tier 2): add a\n  USER_EFFECTIVE_MODULES_SQL next to ENABLED_MODULE_CODES_SQL in permission-catalogue.ts (SSoT:\n  user_module_assignments ura JOIN tenant_modules tm ON tm.\"moduleId\"=ura.\"moduleId\" AND\n  tm.\"tenantId\"=$2 AND tm.\"isEnabled\"=true JOIN modules m ON m.id=ura.\"moduleId\" AND\n  m.\"isActive\"=true WHERE ura.\"userId\"=$1 AND ura.\"isActive\"=true AND (ura.\"expiresAt\" IS NULL OR\n  ura.\"expiresAt\">NOW()), selecting code/name/defaultRoute).
